name: Kreativ Broken Image Finder
description: Catch missing images early and keep content quality high across your site.
cardUse: Catch missing images across posts and pages before users see them.
metaDescription: Detect missing image references across posts and pages before they impact trust and UX.

detailItems.title: A broader image scan
detailItems.body: Scans published posts, pages and public custom post types, including content, excerpts, custom fields and featured images. It checks image references in srcset, lazy-load attributes and CSS URLs, plus Media Library originals and generated sizes.

detailItems.title: An actionable report
detailItems.body: See the affected item, source, field name and response code. Filter or export the report, recheck a repaired item, and ignore selected URLs, domains or items. Verify blocked requests before treating them as missing files.

supportingLinks.label: Read the historical 1.2.0 workflow checks and limitations

items.title: Manual checks, not an automatic schedule
items.body: Scans are started manually in the dashboard or with WP-CLI. Results identify issues for you to review; the plugin does not automatically change content. Images generated only by themes or external services may be outside the scan's scope.

changelog.label: Status refresh
changelog.body: Plugin page copy and public metadata were refreshed to align with the current Kreativ WP maintenance positioning.

changelog.label: Release note link added
changelog.body: The plugin page now points to a dedicated update post so visitors can move from the plugin page into concrete release context.

quickStart: In WordPress, open Plugins → Add New Plugin and search for “Kreativ Broken Image Finder”, or upload the ZIP. Install and activate it on staging first.
Open the Kreativ Broken Image Finder menu and choose “Run Full Scan”. Keep the dashboard open while the batches complete.
Review the summary and filter results by post type, source, or response code. Check the field name for images found in excerpts or custom fields.
Open the affected item and verify the image before repairing it. Blocked requests and temporary errors can need manual review. Save your changes, then use Recheck.
